'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Northern Chad offensive|Northern Chad offensive]]
**[[President of Chad|Chadian President]] [[Idriss Déby]] dies from wounds sustained while commanding forces against rebels in the northern portion of the country. The [[Constitution of Chad|Constitution]] is suspended, and a [[Transitional Military Council (2021)|Transitional Military Council]] headed by Déby's son, General [[Mahamat Déby Itno|Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno]], will rule the country for an estimated 18 months. [https://www.theafricareport.com/81373/chad-president-idriss-deby-dies-says-national-radio/ (''The Africa Report'')]
*[[Greenfield University kidnapping]]
**A group of gunmen [[kidnap]] students from [[Greenfield University]] in [[Kaduna]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/23/nigerian-kidnappers-kill-3-abducted-students-in-rising-violence (Al Jazeera)] 

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****The number of intensive care patients with COVID-19 in [[France]] reaches a high of 5,984 patients. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-04-20/french-people-in-intensive-care-for-covid-19-at-a-2021-high (U.S. News & World Report)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The [[Government of the Netherlands|government]] announces that it will ease strict [[COVID-19]] restrictions, including ending the controversial curfew and allowing cafés to serve in outdoor terraces with a maximum of 50 people beginning April 28. In addition, people will also be allowed to have two guests at home per day. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210420-dutch-to-lift-covid-curfew-let-cafes-serve-outdoors (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]]
****[[Romania]] reports a record 237 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 26,618. [https://www.romania-insider.com/highest-daily-death-roll-romania-covid?fbclid=IwAR2R7ILZHYlw_H-ifuPxk5BpFZDO8njL7OcG86Iq1SwfOzDWfq8BVCVby08 (Romania Insider)]
***The [[Johnson & Johnson]] [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] will resume rollouts in [[Europe]]. [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/j-j-resumes-european-covid-19-vaccine-rollout-with-regulator-mandated-safety-warning-11619010856 (MarketWatch)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports a record 1,761 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 180,530. [https://www.firstpost.com/india/india-registers-259170-new-coronavirus-cases-record-1761-fatalities-in-24-hrs-9547591.html (''Firstpost'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal]]
****[[Nepal]] grants a conditional emergency use approval for the Russian [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] developed by the [[Gamaleya Research Institute of Epidemiology and Microbiology]]. [https://kathmandupost.com/health/2021/04/20/nepal-grants-conditional-emergency-use-approval-to-russian-sputnik-v-vaccine (''The Kathmandu Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Yemen]]
****[[Yemen]] begins their [[COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccination]] campaign using the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] produced by [[AstraZeneca]] and the [[University of Oxford]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSKBN2C723H (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] records its second community transmission case in the daughter of a woman who works at a [[quarantine]] facility and who previously tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/440868/fiji-records-second-community-case-of-covid-19 (Radio New Zealand)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****A worker at [[Auckland Airport]] tests positive a day after the country restarted reciprocal travel to [[Australia]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-56811375 (BBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt]]
***[[Egypt]] signs an agreement to purchase 20 million doses of the [[Sinopharm]] [[BBIBP-CorV]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] and expects a delivery of 500,000 doses this month. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1845781/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
***[[President of Mexico|President]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]] receives his first dose of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/20/lopez-obrador-gets-covid-jab-it-protects-us-all (Al Jazeera English)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***The [[European Medicines Agency]] publishes a report suggesting a "possible link" between usage of the [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine]] candidate and rare [[blood clots]]. The agency maintains, however, that the overall benefits of the vaccine outweigh the risks of side effects. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/health/medical/eu-agency-e2-80-98possible-link-e2-80-99-between-johnson-26-johnson-coronavirus-vaccine-and-rare-blood-clots/ar-BB1fRyiH (U.S. News & World Report via MSN)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Canada–United States relations]], [[Deployment of COVID-19 vaccines]]
**[[Governor of North Dakota|North Dakota Governor]] [[Doug Burgum]] announces that the [[North Dakota|state]] will offer [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s to [[Manitoba]] truck drivers across [[Canada–United States border|the border]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/manitoba-north-dakota-vaccine-essential-workers-1.5994519 (CBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*''[[State v. Chauvin]]''
**Former [[Minneapolis Police Department]] officer [[Derek Chauvin]] is found guilty on all counts in the [[murder of George Floyd]]. He is scheduled to be sentenced on June 25. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/20/us/derek-chauvin-trial-george-floyd-deliberations/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/04/23/derek-chauvin-sentencing-date-set-for-june-after-murder-conviction.html (CNBC)]
*[[Quebec ban on religious symbols]]
**The [[Quebec Superior Court]] overturns certain provisions of Bill 21, which prohibits public sector employees in positions of [[Government of Quebec|authority]] from wearing religious symbols, on the basis that it violates [[Section 3 of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms|Sections 3]] and [[Section 23 of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms|23]] of the ''[[Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms]]''. However, the Court upholds most of the legislation. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/20/bill-21-quebec-court-strikes-down-part-religious-symbols-law (Al Jazeera English)]

'''Sports'''
*[[European Super League|The Super League]]
**Following a massive negative backlash from [[UEFA]], [[FIFA]], national football associations and [[association football|football]] fans alike, all six English [[Premier League]] clubs involved in the project – [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] – officially withdraw from [[European Super League|The Super League]], while [[FC Barcelona]] president [[Joan Laporta]] states that the club will not join the proposed competition without support from its registered members. Manchester United chief executive [[Ed Woodward]] announces his resignation. [https://www.express.co.uk/sport/football/1425707/European-Super-League-LIVE-Man-City-Chelsea-Barcelona-Atletico-Madrid (''Daily Express'')] [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56823501 (BBC Sport)]
**Hundreds of Chelsea fans protest against the club's involvement in [[European Super League|The Super League]] outside the club's stadium [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]]. The Chelsea [[supporters' trust]] denounces the proposed breakaway as the "ultimate betrayal", and "unforgivable". [https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/apr/20/chelsea-fans-protest-against-super-league-as-supporters-unite-in-anger (''The Guardian'')]
